description: Kansas Child Care Assistance helps eligible families pay part of approved childcare costs. The family must use a DCF-enrolled provider.
introduction: Kansas Child Care Assistance helps eligible families pay part of approved childcare costs. The family must use a DCF-enrolled provider.

sections.who: Kansas families may qualify through work, approved education or training, TANF activities, teen-parent schooling or other specified needs. Children generally must be under 13; exceptions exist.
sections.get: DCF issues childcare benefits on the Kansas Benefits Card. The family plan identifies each child, provider, benefit and family copay; assistance may not cover the full provider charge.
sections.docs: Prepare adult identity, household income and children’s birth/citizenship evidence. Include the work or education schedule and provider information requested for the childcare plan.
sections.apply:
1. Apply through the DCF Self-Service Portal or request a paper application at 888-369-4777. Respond to requests for additional information.

  2. Choose a DCF-enrolled provider. Child Care Aware of Kansas, 877-678-2548, can help identify providers; ask about openings and any uncovered charges before signing an agreement.
sections.after: Read the approved family plan and reporting instructions. Coordinate payments with the provider and inform DCF when the arrangement changes.
sections.sources:
Application and program details: DCF childcare eligibility and application, Provider payment rules.

Historical screenshots and background: USA Assistance. Screenshots may show an earlier application interface.

faqs: No. The provider must be enrolled with DCF.
Will DCF necessarily pay the whole bill?
No. Check the benefit, copay and provider charges.
The usual age rule is under 13, but specified exceptions may apply.
Is foster childcare handled the same way?
DCF links a separate Foster Care Child Care application; ask which route applies.
